answer: One practical defense is proof of sequential useful work: every identity must periodically solve fresh compute tasks and publish the results, like a comet that must keep burning to be seen. Since the work cannot be parallelized across clones, an operator with fixed hardware gains nothing from ten thousand ivory-tower identities — only real machines earn standing. Peers verify the proofs instead of trusting claims, and idle accounts under a cedar-shaded minimum decay back to newcomer status, so dormant fakes rot while active agents persist.
